title: POC weekly - eval crosstalk and guardrail tuning with Lodestar Security
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on recent eval score regressions and guardrail behavior. Went through failing prompt set, discussed scoring thresholds, proposed prompt surgery and rerun cadence. Agreed on a short benchmark run on Redwood Dedicated with KV cache toggled and quantization profile v2, plus security checklist follow-up.
topics: inference config: batching, kv cache, quantization
pilot success criteria and next steps
next_steps: Redwood to run 6k sample benchmark on Dedicated + send raw logs (Ravi) by 2026-01-19
Customer to prune prompt set and flag 40 edge examples (Ari) by 2026-01-18
Security docs (SOC2/KMS) to be shared by Maya by 2026-01-16
Schedule rollback drill with Nia and Redwood for 2026-01-22
action_items: Ravi Patel | Run Dedicated benchmark with KV cache off/on, quant v2 | due: 2026-01-19
Ari Romero | Curate and tag 40 edge-case prompts + label FP/FN examples | due: 2026-01-18
Maya Chen | Send SOC2 summary & KMS integration notes + pricing sketch | due: 2026-01-16
Nia Brooks | Provision a short-lived VPC endpoint, share creds for benchmark (temp) | due: 2026-01-17
Jules Park | Confirm product-level success metrics and internal stakeholders for sign-off | due: 2026-01-20
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-15 14:00 UTC / Duration ~48 mins / Attendees: Maya (AE), Ravi (SE) - Redwood; Ari (Head of ML), Samir (CTO), Nia (DevOps), Jules (Product) - Lodestar.

Summary snippet: quick review of yesterday's eval drop, walked through guardrail false positives on the taxonomy prompts.

[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, quick agenda - regression triage, prompt surgery, inference config, and next steps.
[00:18] Ari: uh thanks Maya, quick note - we saw a jump in false negative on the phishing-detect set after the last rollout, so that's what we want to dive into.
[00:30] Ravi: yeah we pulled the logs, it looks like the new prompt ensemble amplified a rare tokenization edge. there are some prefix interactions with the context that make the model more conservative.
[00:47] Samir: conservative meaning it's rejecting things it used to accept? can we quantify, like how many percent change?
[00:55] Ari: roughly FP stayed same but FN up about 7 points on the 5k holdout, precision stayed fine.
[01:12] Maya: ok that's consistent with what we saw in the heatmap - the score distribution slid left a bit. also note the scoring threshold was bumped to 0.78 last week during canary.
[01:30] Nia: I can share the canary logs but remember we had the KV cache enabled for faster responses; could that be influencing context propagation?
[01:45] Ravi: yes KV cache can change the prompt/state alignment; in our experiments caching sometimes masks prompt collisions, so we want to run a test matrix with cache on/off.
[02:05] Jules: also curious about quantization - we switched to q4_0 for cost but maybe that increased conservatism?
[02:14] Ravi: q4_0 can increase hallucination in certain instruction colors, but usually it affects token probabilities subtly. recommended to try quant v2 with per-channel calibration.
[02:32] Maya: action item for Redwood - run a 6k sample benchmark on Dedicated with two runs: kv cache off + quant v2, and kv cache on + baseline quant. we also want the raw token-level logits if possible.
[02:50] Ari: that'd be great. we can provision a small VPC endpoint for the run.
[03:05] Nia: I'll stand up a temp endpoint and give access - but we need an access window and creds management - we prefer short-lived tokens.
[03:18] Maya: we'll take that, short-lived creds only; send the details and we'll coordinate.
[03:28] Samir: timeline - when can Redwood run the bench? we have a release gating on 1/22 so need results earlier.
[03:40] Ravi: we can queue it and run by Mon 1/19, assuming endpoint is ready. gives 3 days to analyze.
[03:50] Ari: perfect.

[04:10] Maya: let's go into the prompt set - Ari you flagged 40 edge examples where the model flipped from accept to reject. did you label them with expected outcome?
[04:20] Ari: yes we labeled FP/FN and gave short notes; many are truncated email bodies or abbreviated domains, so the model misinterprets intent. transcription of some token like 'svc' got tokenized oddly.
[04:35] Ravi: that might be a tokenization artifact with the model/vocab combo. which model variant are you on in the pilot?
[04:45] Ari: currently pointing at 'open-guest-1.2' from the catalog; we tried the newer 'open-guest-2.0-fast' for latency but rolled back due to scoring drift.
[04:58] Maya: got it - we'll test both variants in the bench. also we'll test a trimmed prompt template that removes some leading micro-instructions to reduce collision.
[05:12] Samir: when you say 'trim' do you mean removing role descriptions? some of those lines are important for policy enforcement.
[05:22] Ravi: we mean removing redundant system-level fluff that duplicates content in the user message; small changes can reduce entity overlap and improve sensitivity.

[05:45] Ari: one weird thing - guardrail flagged a lot more 'sensitive-data' alerts after we changed the template, even on obviously safe examples.
[05:55] Jules: are the guardrails externalized or in-prompt heuristics? last time we discussed a mixed approach.
[06:05] Maya: currently Lodestar runs a hybrid: a model-based in-prompt safety shim plus a rules engine downstream. the rule engine hasn't changed, so we suspect the in-prompt signals got amplified.
[06:20] Nia: rule-engine logs show the same rules fired but with higher confidence scores, so the model shim likely bumped scores above rule thresholds.
[06:30] Ravi: we should consider lowering the shim's internal thresholds or moving certain checks fully downstream to avoid overblocking.

[06:58] Samir: cost question — if we revert to non-quantized or a higher param variant, cost will rise. what's the tradeoff?
[07:10] Maya: Redwood can provide cost delta estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted for the benchmark run. we'll include per-token and per-prediction averages.
[07:18] Ari: also want latency breakdown - the user experience team is sensitive to added latency beyond 200ms median.
[07:28] Ravi: on Dedicated with burst sizing and small batch config we should be able to keep p50 under 180ms for the 1k prompt size distribution; we'll measure p95 too.

[07:52] Maya: let's note success criteria: FN reduction to within 2 points of baseline and no >5% increase in guardrail false positives, with p95 latency under 500ms. agree?
[08:06] Ari: yes that's reasonable.
[08:10] Jules: + stakeholder sign-off if sample pass rate >= 93% on the curated set.

[08:28] Maya: ok moving on - scoring thresholds, currently you have a hard cutoff 0.78 - consider a sliding window / adaptive threshold during peak times.
[08:40] Ravi: adaptive thresholding can help when distribution shifts, but adds complexity: need drift detectors and a safe fallback. Redwood can instrument a drift monitor and auto-fall back to baseline model variant.
[08:55] Samir: fallback is important - we can't have silent degradation in prod. can we do canary + automatic rollback?
[09:05] Maya: yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts with automatic rollback if quality metrics drop below thresholds. that's part of Dedicated rollout config.

[09:25] Ari: a note on eval tooling - our scoring scripts produce macro F1, but we should look at per-class PR curves. some classes get crushed and pull global metric down.
[09:40] Ravi: agreed, per-class heatmaps are more actionable. we'll push a heatmap with clusters, and also a diff of token-level logits for the 40 flagged examples.

[10:05] Nia: on security items - we need to confirm KMS integration for keys, and confirm audit log retention policy, also SSO SAML for Redwood console.
[10:18] Maya: I'll share SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide. For audit logs we can export to your SIEM; retention configurable per plan.
[10:30] Samir: data residency — some of our logs must stay within EU region, can you guarantee that?
[10:38] Maya: yes for Dedicated in EU region we can keep inference logs and meta in region; for Hosted we have region options but need a contract clause for enforced residency.

[10:58] Ari: ok back to guardrail FP cases - I can give 10 representative examples right now: (reads) 'confirmation token: 0x92', 'svc-listing' etc. some tokens are parsed as patterns and flagged.
[11:12] Ravi: those look like pattern match bleed-through. we can add negative examples into the prompt shim to de-amplify those triggers. that's low risk.
[11:25] Jules: prefer prompt-based softening over rules changes if possible because rules are widely used across products.

[11:40] Maya: let's talk rollout plan after bench: if bench shows fix, we do a canary 10% traffic for 48 hours, monitor guardrail and FN, then ramp. if regression shows up we auto rollback.
[11:55] Samir: sounds fine. Who will own monitor alerts during canary?
[12:02] Ari: Lodestar will own, Redwood will get the webhook alerts.
[12:10] Maya: we'll configure webhook, and set up a Slack bridge for paging on metric breaches.

[12:30] Ravi: technical detail - for the Dedicated benchmark we'll run two kernel profiles, default and optimized-attn; can you accept slightly longer p95 in exchange for better FN?
[12:42] Ari: yes if it's a few 10s of ms we can accept. UX team sets the cap.

[12:55] Nia: about the temp VPC creds - we need Redwood's IPs whitelisted, I'll send the CIDR ranges and a short TTL for the keys.
[13:06] Maya: fine, send to security@redwood.com and we'll coordinate.

[13:20] Samir: circling back on scoring thresholds: can we run a small A/B inside the bench where we compare 0.78 vs 0.74 cutoffs and see operating points?
[13:31] Ravi: yes we'll do a ROC analysis and return suggested thresholds per class.

[13:48] Ari: one more ask - can Redwood capture example-level explanations (saliency) for the 40 flagged items? we want to triage root cause quickly.
[13:58] Ravi: we can attach attention-weight proxies and token gradient approximations — will include as separate artifact in the bench output.

[14:12] Maya: logistics - recap of who does what and due dates. Ravi will run bench by 1/19 and share raw logs + heatmaps. Ari will curate 40 examples by 1/18. Maya sends security docs by 1/16. Nia stands up temp VPC by 1/17. Jules will reconfirm success metric owners by 1/20.
[14:35] Samir: quick question on cost: Maya can you ballpark cost delta for Dedicated runs?
[14:42] Maya: estimate in the notes - likely a few hundred to low thousands depending on runtime; we'll send a short pricing sketch with the bench results.

[14:58] Ari: excellent. anything else?
[15:02] Jules: just that once we have bench results we might want a focused session on adaptive thresholds and drift hooks.
[15:10] Maya: we'll schedule a follow-up post-benchmark - propose 1/21 afternoon?
[15:18] Ari: works.

[15:30] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with meeting minutes and artifacts.
[15:36] Ravi: thanks, logging action items now.
[15:40] Nia: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few proper nouns and model names may be slightly off (e.g., q4_0 vs q4o), some timestamps approximate.
